hookLine: On the afternoon of Sunday the twelfth of February, twenty seventeen, a woman named Denise

lines: THIS IS WHAT THE COURT SAID THAT WAS WORTH.

ACT_1.secondary: The tallest dam in the United States holds back the Feather River above the town.
Evacuation of 'the low levels of Oroville and areas downstream.' The county's words, to the minute.

ACT_1.quote: [O]fficials now anticipate a failure of the Auxiliary Spillway at Oroville Dam within the next 60 minutes.
ACT_1.attribution: Butte County's second broadcast, approx. 4:34 p.m.

ACT_1.secondary: Evacuation of all Yuba County on the valley floor.
Immediate evacuation: Live Oak, Yuba City, Nicolaus, and other communities along the Feather River.
Denise Johnson was walking in when the shop announced it was closing for a mandatory evacuation — her sworn declaration.
Francis Bechtel saw a mandatory evacuation order on his screen an hour and ten minutes before the county's first order. Why is not explained in anything retrieved.

ACT_1.label: Minutes after the broadcast, a sheriff's vehicle came down his street announcing that residents had to leave — his declaration

ACT_1.quote: It was just panic. People were running in the streets. Cars were speeding.
ACT_1.attribution: Genoa Widener, Oroville resident, contemporaneous press interview

ACT_1.secondary: No flood reached a town. Nobody died and nobody was hurt. The film says so now, on purpose.
The orders were reduced to a warning. Two days.

ACT_2.secondary: A section of concrete eroded from the middle of the main spillway. DWR's own photograph is timestamped.
Water flowed over the emergency spillway. DWR's own video of that afternoon exists.
Friends of the River, the Sierra Club and the South Yuba River Citizens League file a motion with federal regulators about this exact spillway.

ACT_2.quote: We urged them to put concrete on the spillway – our argument was that without a proper spillway, this could happen.
ACT_2.attribution: Ron Stork, policy director, Friends of the River

ACT_2.quote: It was a slow moving crisis that picked up a lot of speed yesterday.
ACT_2.attribution: Ron Stork, Friends of the River

ACT_2.primary: WHAT THIS FILM DOES NOT SAY
ACT_2.secondary: 'Officials ignored warnings' is a headline's characterisation. No tribunal has found it. The filing is a fact; the verdict on it is nobody's yet.

ACT_2.label: Years between the 2005 motion and the February 2017 orders — our arithmetic, from the record's dates

ACT_2.secondary: The federal docket the 2005 motion lives in. The motion itself was not retrieved; this film quotes nothing from it.
Counties issued the orders. The lawsuit's defendant is the State, through the Department of Water Resources. The two are not the same and this film never blurs them.

ACT_3.secondary: Shelters stood at fairgrounds in surrounding unaffected areas — Chico among them. The state's own after-action report.

ACT_3.quote: Many of the people, especially low income, ran out with just the shirts on their backs.
ACT_3.attribution: Bob Mulholland, volunteer, Silver Dollar Fairgrounds shelter

ACT_3.secondary: Kaysi and Greg Levias, two boys and a dog, had moved in three weeks earlier. What didn't fit in the car they piled as high as they could.
Nicoli Nicholas moved hundreds of cattle, tons of baled hay and his equipment out of Sutter County — the complaint's account.

ACT_3.label: Dollars, at least, in relocation and return costs for the ranch — the complaint's figure, stated as an allegation

ACT_3.secondary: On the rented pastures the cows caught a virus; back home, their newborn calves were infected — the complaint's account.

ACT_3.label: Rental homes directly downstream in which Jeanette Morton alleges a loss of value

ACT_3.secondary: A brewing company closed for about a week — roughly ten thousand dollars, its CFO estimated, and slow to come back.
Two day-care centres — one for ages two to five, one for under-threes — forced to suspend business. The complaint's account.
Jeanette Morton files a claim with the State under Government Code section 910. The paperwork begins.

ACT_4.secondary: Approximately 188,000 residents of Oroville, Marysville, Yuba City and other areas near the Feather River who were ordered to evacuate.
Out-of-pocket expenses for the two-day evacuation, and the value of the lost days — not the dam, not the spillway, the two days.
Ninety pages. Two plaintiff groups denied class status. Only Bechtel appealed.

ACT_4.quote: There is simply no means by which to readily determine whether a residence or person falls within a 'mandatory' evacuation zone.
ACT_4.attribution: the trial court's class-certification ruling, as quoted by the Court of Appeal

ACT_4.quote: In fact, the evidence and briefing submitted to the trial court demonstrated there was no defined mandatory evacuation zone and no defined voluntary evacuation zone.
ACT_4.attribution: Bechtel v. Department of Water Resources, Cal. Ct. App., Third District, 15 March 2022 (unpublished)

ACT_4.secondary: 'Low levels of Oroville and areas downstream.' The orders' own words, read back by the court as the reason no class can exist.
Dr. Cova, an expert on human evacuations: the decision to evacuate is left to each household. There is no known method to count who left.
DWR argued below that even a 'mandatory' evacuation was not actually mandatory — there is no penalty for ignoring the order.

lines: AND NO ONE CAN SAY WHO.

ACT_4.quote: This lack of ascertainability would also prevent individual class members from self-identifying as meeting the class definition.
ACT_4.attribution: Bechtel v. Department of Water Resources, Cal. Ct. App., Third District, 15 March 2022 (unpublished)

ACT_4.quote: [B]ecause there simply is no typical claim among this group, the Court cannot say that the proposed Plaintiffs have claims typical of the class.
ACT_4.attribution: the trial court's class-certification ruling, as quoted by the Court of Appeal

ACT_4.secondary: The judgment is affirmed. The Department of Water Resources shall recover its costs on appeal.

ACT_5.secondary: The opinion is marked unpublished. California's rules prohibit citing it. The rule that decided 188,000 people's case binds nobody else.
What the evacuation cost her appears nowhere in anything retrieved. The record does not say. So neither does this film.

ACT_5.primary: 5 OCTOBER 2023 — THE CASE THAT DID WIN
ACT_5.secondary: The same Court of Appeal holds DWR liable — in the action the Butte County District Attorney brought over the river itself.

ACT_5.primary: READ THE WINNING OPINION FOR THE PEOPLE
ACT_5.secondary: 27,810 characters. 'Evacuate' appears zero times. 'Resident' appears zero times. The win belongs to the fish.
No settlement, verdict or judgment for an individual evacuee was found in any source retrieved. An established absence.

ACT_5.label: Pages of scanned government claim forms, public, their names too degraded to read
Pages in the trial-court ruling that ended the class — a ruling not retrievable from any open source tried

ACT_5.secondary: The other two class representatives. Their declarations were not retrieved; the film tells this story in two voices, and says so.

ACT_5.primary: THE ONES WHO DID NOT APPEAL
ACT_5.secondary: Marie Giordano, above the dam with three rentals downstream, and the Giordano plaintiffs: denied alongside Bechtel, and their case ended there.

events.label: regulators asked to line the spillway

lines: THE REMEDY WAS FOR NO ONE.

ENDING.secondary: An order vague enough to move 188,000 people can be too vague to owe any one of them anything.

_readme: SP-04 IS LOAD-BEARING: an ACT_1 card states on screen that the dam did not fail and nobody was hurt, before any legal beat. Nothing later may imply otherwise.
OR-07: the issuers-vs-defendant card is in ACT_2 so the viewer carries the distinction into the courtroom acts. No card calls the counties defendants or DWR the issuer.
FR-05: the 2005 filing is carded as a filing plus Stork's own words. The 'ignored warnings' characterisation appears only inside the card that disclaims it.
DJ-06 / GC-02 / CL-04 are ABSENCES and are carded as absences -- the film's honesty is that the record runs out, and the cards say so instead of papering over it.
AF-03: the fish card quotes the grep result (zero occurrences) exactly as measured.
MONEY FIGURES ($150,000, ~$10,000, six homes) are attributed to the complaint or the speaker on the card itself; none is stated as a court finding.
